codePrompt: : enter the code from your authenticator app.
enrollPrompt: The panel requires a second sign-in factor. Set up an authenticator app for the account
login.recoveryUsed_one: A recovery code was used – {{count}} left. Generate new ones in “Account security”.
login.recoveryUsed_other: A recovery code was used – {{count}} left. Generate new ones in “Account security”.
login.orCode: or a code from the app
login.keyCancelled: Sign-in with the key was interrupted – try again or enter a code.

mfa.step1: Install an authenticator app on your phone, e.g. Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator or Aegis.
mfa.step2: Add an account by scanning the QR code (or enter the key manually).
mfa.step3: Enter the 6-digit code shown by the app below.
mfa.qrAlt: QR code for setting up the authenticator app
mfa.codeOrRecovery: Code from the app or a recovery code
mfa.fileHeader:
Vardr – recovery codes for the second sign-in factor
Each code works once.
mfa.saveText: Each code lets you sign in once without your phone (lost, out of battery). Keep them safe, e.g. in a password manager.
mfa.saveOnce: They will not be shown again.
mfa.savedCheck: I have saved the recovery codes

password.title: Change password
password.intro: At least {{min}} characters; a few easy-to-remember words work best.
password.introForced: You are signed in with an initial password – set your own before continuing.
password.newHint: at least {{min}} characters, without the username
password.changed: Password changed. Other sessions of this account were ended.

security.title: Account security
security.intro: Second sign-in factor: after the password the panel asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone, so a stolen password alone is not enough to sign in.
security.unavailable: The second factor is not configured on the server (no MFA key) – tell your administrator.

policy.all: In this panel the second factor is required for all accounts
policy.admins: In this panel the second factor is required for administrators
policy.none: In this panel the second factor is optional

security.fewCodes: Few recovery codes left – generate new ones.
security.oldCodesInvalid: Your existing recovery codes will stop working.
security.disableWarning: Without a second factor the password alone is enough to sign in. The account's security keys will be removed too.
security.ssoText: The second sign-in factor is confirmed by the identity provider – Entra ID administrators set it up (e.g. Conditional Access). The panel authenticator app is not used for this account.
security.ssoSessionMfa: Current session: signed in with a second factor.
security.ssoSessionNoMfa: Current session: the provider did not confirm a second factor.

keys.title: Security keys and passkeys
keys.intro: A hardware key (YubiKey, Titan…), Windows Hello, Touch ID or a passkey on your phone instead of the app code – touch the key when signing in. Phishing-resistant: the key works only at this panel address. The authenticator app and recovery codes stay as the fallback.
keys.totpFirst: Enable the authenticator app (above) first – it stays as the fallback when the key is not at hand.
keys.needsName: Keys work only when the panel is opened by name (e.g. https://vardr.company.com:8444), not by IP address.
keys.unsupported: This browser does not support security keys (or the page is not opened over HTTPS).
keys.name: Name
keys.otherAddress: registered for {{rp}} – works only at that address
keys.touch: After clicking, the browser asks you to insert and touch the key (or Windows Hello / Touch ID).
keys.cancelled: Adding the key was interrupted (or the key is already registered).
keys.removeText: Remove the key "{{name}}"? Signing in with it will stop working; the authenticator app stays.
